details.description: Ministral 3 8B Instruct 2512 is Mistral AI's 8.4B-parameter instruction-tuned model from the Ministral 3 family, released December 2, 2025, paired with a 0.4B-parameter vision encoder for native image understanding. Released under the Apache 2.0 license, it targets efficient edge and local deployment -- Mistral says it fits in 12GB of VRAM in FP8, less when further quantized, and can run on a single H200 GPU -- with a 256K-token context window, native function calling, JSON output, and native multilingual and multimodal support. It sits in the middle of the Ministral 3 lineup, between the 3B and 14B sizes.
advantages: Scores 87.6% on MATH Maj@1 and an Arena Hard score of 50.9, per Mistral's published instruct benchmark table.
Scores 66.8 on WildBench and 8.08 on MM MTBench (multimodal chat), per the same instruct benchmark table.
Includes a native 0.4B-parameter vision encoder for image understanding alongside the 8.4B-parameter language model.
Supports native function calling, JSON-constrained output, and both explicit and implicit prompt caching.
Released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license, allowing commercial use and modification.
disadvantages: Mistral's deployment guidance recommends temperatures well under 0.1 for production use, which its model card notes can limit performance on creative tasks that benefit from more temperature exploration.
use_cases: Local chat interfaces and on-device AI assistants
Agentic applications using function calling and tool use
Base for custom fine-tuning and post-training

notes: Catalog's max_output_tokens equals max_input_tokens (262,144); no source opened states a separate max-output limit distinct from the 256K context window, so the catalog figure was kept as-is. The Hugging Face model card has separate benchmark tables for the Base, Instruct and Reasoning variants of the 8B size; the evaluation scores above were taken only from the Instruct table to match this exact model (Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512). Mistral names 'English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic' as example supported languages ('dozens' total, '40+' per the family announcement) without a closed list, so the languages field was left empty rather than presenting a partial list as complete.
